steps: Plan the design option
Choose standard, vented cavity, Komfort Zone Kit, heat transfer kit(s) or Kozy Power Vent before framing — framing, mantel and trim rules differ. Convert to propane or for the #KPV before framing in.

The design option sets the framing, mantel and trim rules, so decide it before you frame.

  • Standard installation: follow the sections marked 'standard installation'. Standard framing still applies with heat transfer kits (HTK-EXT / HTK-INT): up to 2 kits, remove 1 square rear cover plate per kit.
  • Vented cavity: a minimum-size air discharge opening in the fireplace cavity for heat reduction above the fireplace — allows combustible facing materials above, heat reduction for a TV above, and lower mantel clearances (section 3.8).
  • Komfort Zone Kit (#KZK-038 or #KZK-1510A): redistributes radiant heat through plenum(s); framing may differ — follow the kit manual.
  • Kozy Power Vent #KPV: fan-powered mechanical draft, horizontal terminations only.

Fireplace chamber and ceiling minimum height: 88" for all design options. Install on a level surface that supports the fireplace and venting, out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies; it may be installed in a bedroom. It is heavy — team lift, using the lift handles on both sides or a 2" x 4" through them.

Convert to propane, or for the #KPV, before framing in. Doing either after installation means removing the control board (section 8.5).

Outdoor covered installs (section 3.6): operation approved from 40°F to 110°F; the overhang in front and to each side must be at least 1/2 of the roofline height above the fireplace base; black painted safety barriers highly recommended.
Nailing flanges & stand-offs

Fit both nailing flanges (they give the minimum 3½" side clearance to framing), then form and fit the stand-off assembly, header heat shield and back stand-off heat shields before the unit goes in the opening.

1. Remove the 2 nailing flanges from the sides. Align them with the holes on the outside corners, stand-off flanges facing away from the fireplace, and secure with the screws provided through the slots.
  2. Bend the perforation until parallel with the fireplace face — not toward it. Framing studs sit against the small stand-off on the back of each flange; the flanges give the minimum 3½" clearance from the sides of the fireplace to framing.
  3. Form the header heat shield and attach it to the stand-off assembly (4 screws). Align the stand-off assembly with the holes on top of the fireplace and secure it (4 screws).
  4. Remove and save the back stand-off bracket screws, form the back stand-off heat shields and resecure them with those screws.
Nailing flanges must be installed for all applications and never permanently removed. The stand-off assembly and header heat shield must be installed to keep standard-installation clearances.

Vented cavity / Komfort Zone Kit: remove the 2 top cover plates (4 screws each) and the convection baffle. The header heat shield may be removed; the top stand-off assembly and back stand-offs stay (sections 3.7.2 and 3.7.2.1).
Rough framing & vent rough-in
Frame the enclosure to Figure 3.5 (the same for all design options), 88" minimum height; keep 1" around the vent pipe and 17-1/8" from any venting to the enclosure top on horizontal terminations.

• Rough-in dimensions are drawn in Figure 3.5 (p. 15); they are the same for all design options and must be followed. This is a cold air transfer area — insulate outside walls.
  • Set the fireplace directly on wood or a non-combustible surface, not linoleum or carpet. On carpet, tile or other combustible material other than wood flooring, install it on a metal or wood panel the full width and depth of the appliance.
  • Floor protection in front isn't required; a hearth extension may be combustible and may be flush with the bottom finishing edge.
  • Raised installs need a solid, continuous platform and must keep ceiling clearances; masonry needs a foundation for the full load.
  • Vent pipe: 1" on all sides of vertical pipe and on the top, sides and bottom of horizontal pipe; 17-1/8" from any venting to the enclosure top in all horizontal terminations.
  • Horizontal runs: 1/4" rise per 12" of travel; wall thimbles that keep the 1" top clearance at every interior or exterior wall; never recess the cap into wall or siding. A Metal Fab adapter raises the minimum vent-centre height by 3-1/4".
  • Wall pass-through: measure from the fireplace floor level to the vent centre — Figure 3.7 (p. 17) gives the minimum horizontal-termination dimension with a Simpson DuraVent elbow; other elbows vary.

TV above: tests found TV surface temperatures did not exceed 150°F with a 4¼" deep recess above the fireplace. TV location rests with the homeowner.
Facing & finishing
Non-combustible facing (up to 1/2" thick) at the top and sides, run only to the finishing edge so the glass frame stays removable; hold the mantel and sidewall clearances.

• Non-combustible material is required at the top and sides; the fireplace takes non-combustible facing up to 1/2" thick (minimum finishing dimensions: Figure 4.5, p. 37).
  • Install facing up to the finishing edge around the glass frame assembly and no further. The glass frame assembly must be removable.
  • Pre-drilling and self-tapping screws are acceptable; screws may penetrate the outer shell only up to 1/2", in the allowed areas.
  • Combustible mantel: 3/4" trim from 12" above the top finishing edge; a 6" mantel from 15-1/2"; above that, 1" more depth for every 1" of height.
  • Non-combustible mantel: 6" minimum above the top finishing edge, up to 6" deep; then 1" up for every 1" deeper.
  • Side trim: 1" combustible projection from 3" off the side finishing edge, unlimited after the first 6". Adjacent sidewall: 6". Combustible hearth: may be flush with the bottom finishing edge.
  • To limit drywall cracking: dry, dust-free materials; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound (such as Durabond), cured per the maker; high-quality acrylic latex primer and finish coat — avoid flat or light-colored paints.

The safety barrier screen #BH38-ES sets its notched tabs into the slots on the glass valance (flush or recessed mount). The optional rectangle surround #BH38-RS must be attached before fireplace installation (4 screws).

Vented cavity and Komfort Zone Kit installs use section 4.3 instead: side trim may be flush with the side finishing edge, and combustible wall finish up to 1" thick may go over the required non-combustible material, down to the finishing edge and up to the air discharge opening.
Gas line connection

Qualified installer only (a licensed plumber or gas fitter in Massachusetts). Connect a listed 1/2" tee-handle shut-off and flexible connector to the 1/2" control valve inlet, routed clear of the fan; leak-check with soapy water.

• Install per local building codes, or ANSI Z223.1 where there are none.
  • Supplied with the fireplace: a 3/8" x 24" flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve. A listed (and Massachusetts-approved) 1/2" tee-handle manual shut-off valve and flexible connector connect to the 1/2" control valve inlet; if substituting, check local codes.
  • Bring the line in through the gas line access hole (Figure 2.1, p. 9) to the point where the shut-off valve and flex line connect. Don't run it where it would obstruct fan operation.
  • Supply-piping pressure tests: above ½ psi, disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve; at ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water.
  • Inlet supply: natural gas 5" – 10.5" WC (7" recommended); propane 12" – 13" WC. High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or the authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
Venting & restrictor plate
Run an approved 5" x 8" co-axial system (or reduce to 4" x 6-5/8") within the vertical, horizontal or combination limits; fit or modify the restrictor plate in the 5" exhaust for flame appearance.

• Approved 5" x 8" and 4" x 6-5/8" systems and caps: Tables 7.1 and 7.2 (p. 46). Configurations are shown with rigid pipe; listed flexible systems follow the vent maker's instructions.
  • Vertical: 3' minimum to 50' maximum. Horizontal: 24" vertical allows up to 24" horizontal, 36" up to 8', 48" up to 12', 25' up to 25'. Combination: 25' rise + 25' run = 50' total (elbow allowances in the Venting spec).
  • Horizontal sections need 1/4" rise per 12" of travel. Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.

Restrictor plate (components packet)

Restricts the 5" exhaust to get the desired flame appearance. It ships with both inner rings intact (most restriction); knocking out the innermost ring gives less restriction, the outer ring the least. Bend the tabs to about 80° and slide it into the exhaust pipe on top of the fireplace, tabs facing you, before attaching venting — or through the firebox baffle once venting is attached. Adjustment guidance: section 11.2.2 (p. 72).
Panels & log set
Install the refractory or black glass panels (required to operate), then the 10-piece log set on its studs and pins, with crushed glass, charred pieces, lava rock and rockwool embers.

1. Remove the safety screen, glass assembly and any logs. Separate the 4 panel clips at the perforations and bend each metal finger to 90°.
  2. Refractory (Chicago brick, Ledgestone or Herringbone): back panel first, then the side panels, secured with the bent panel clips and provided screws.
  3. Black glass: wear clean gloves and use both hands; the smooth side faces forward. Back panel first, then slide each side panel along the main log support to the back of the firebox; check the glass sits flat against the firebox.
  4. Logs (#BH38-500 traditional or #BH38-B501 birchwood, same placement): logs 1–5 on the burner studs; log 6 on the pin in log 3, log 7 on log 1, log 8 on log 4, log 9 on log 6; set log 10 as in Figure 8.9.
  5. Crushed glass media into the ember bed media tray; 4 charred pieces on the ember bed; lava rock at the sides onto the media tray braces and firebox floor; brush rockwool embers onto logs and burners with a stiff or steel bristle nylon brush.
Never operate without a refractory or black glass panel kit installed. Don't place logs over burner portholes — it affects flame appearance and builds soot on logs and glass. Convert to propane before installing panels or logs.
Electrical
Supply the junction box with 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps — hot at all times, no switch — and plug into a grounded three-prong receptacle; fit the ember bed and top light halogen bulbs.

• Shut off the household breaker before working on electrical lines. Ground per local codes, or ANSI/NFPA 70 (CSA C22.1 in Canada); never cut or remove the grounding prong.
  • Junction box (4 outlets, left side, behind the electrical access cover's 4 screws): outlets for the Kozy Power Vent, the ember bed light kit and the control module.
  • Ember bed light kit: remove the safety screen, glass frame and media tray; fit the 4 halogen bulbs from the component packet; reinstall.
  • Top light kit #600-TLK: remove the safety screen and glass frame, then the top light cover assembly (8 screws, save them); fit the 2 halogen bulbs; reinstall. Wiring: Figure 9.5 (p. 62).
  • Disconnect all power first, and never touch halogen bulbs with bare hands — use a soft cloth. Convert to propane before installing light kit components.

Battery backup (4 AA) runs the burner only; the fan, top light and ember bed light need AC power. Wiring schematic: Figure 9.1 (p. 60).
Initialize the control

Clear packaging from the firebox; rocker switch OFF; 4 AA backup and 3 AAA remote batteries; AC power on; press the sync button (3 beeps, amber LED), then the remote's ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps).

1. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox.
  2. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF.
  3. Install 4 AA batteries (not included) in the backup battery holder on the control module, and the 3 AAA batteries (components packet) in the remote's battery bay.
  4. Connect the IFC module to AC power.
  5. Lift off the safety barrier screen. Press the remote sync button on the left side: the module beeps 3 times and lights an amber LED.
  6. Within 5 seconds, press ON/OFF on the remote. The receiver beeps 4 times and the pilot lights automatically (the igniter sparks repeatedly; the pilot lights if gas is supplied).
  7. Press ON/OFF again — the pilot goes out, confirming the remote. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote operation and refit the screen.

Then choose IPI or CPI from the remote (section 10.9.3). Running without the remote — main burner on HI only, switched by the rocker — is set up per section 10.3.
Pressure test & flame check

Check inlet pressure at the IN tap (other gas appliances running) and manifold pressure at the OUT tap. Then reseal each tap: turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose, tighten the screw clockwise (snug, don't over-tighten), then relight and confirm with the manometer that the tap is sealed (it should read no pressure). Let it burn 15 minutes, then set the venturis or restrictor plate from the flame appearance.

• Inlet (IN tap, A): manometer on a 1/4" I.D. hose; light pilot and burner; natural gas 5" – 10.5", propane 12" – 13" WC. Then turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose and tighten the screw clockwise (snug, don't over-tighten). Relight pilot and burner, then reattach the manometer and confirm the tap is completely sealed: it should read no pressure.
  • Manifold (OUT tap, B): natural gas 1.1" – 3.8", propane 2.9" – 11" WC (low – high). Then turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the manometer hose and tighten the screw clockwise (snug, don't over-tighten). Relight pilot and burner and attach the manometer to the tap to verify it is completely sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.
  • First-lit flames are blue and should gradually turn yellow over the first 15 minutes. Let it burn 15 minutes before judging, and let it cool before making any adjustment.
  • Venturi (qualified service technician only): remove the screen, glass frame, media tray and the log rack flange (5 screws); loosen the venturi bracket screws. Sliding right opens the air shutter (more air), left closes it (less air). Factory openings: natural gas 1/8", propane 3/8", front and rear — check with the air shutter tool in the components packet. Dark orange flames with black tips: open slightly. Short blue or lifting flames: close. Small moves make dramatic changes.
  • Vent restriction: short, flickering flames (excessive draft) — add the restrictor plate; lifting or ghosting (insufficient draft) — remove inner ring(s) or the plate. If flames still lift after opening the plate and verifying the vent, shut off the gas and call a qualified service technician.
  • Soot on the logs: check log placement before adjusting the venturis.

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power or use battery backup
Wiring disconnection → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas supply off → check each shut-off valve between the appliance and the main line
No propane, or low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → refill; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot flame not enveloping the flame sensor → adjust the pilot screw on the valve (clockwise lowers, counterclockwise raises)
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten

panels.title: Main burner won't light
items: ON/OFF rocker switch in OFF → switch to ON
Gas supply off or low → check for multiple shut-offs; check the propane tank
Faulty or incorrect wiring → see section 9.0
Plugged main burner orifice → remove blockage
Pilot flame not directed to ignite the burner → see the pilot checks
Remote batteries low, or no call for heat → replace batteries; remote ON with thermostat operation OFF

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: No propane in tank → refill
Glass assembly installed incorrectly → section 8.1
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust or clear debris
Horizontal venting without 1/4" rise per 12" of travel
Exhaust leaking back into the firebox → find and repair
Excessive draft → install or modify the restrictor (section 11.2.2)

panels.title: Soot on glass, or blue lifting flames
items: Soot: improper log placement → section 8.4
Soot: venturi air shutter may need opening slightly (more air)
Blue flame lifting off the burner: venturi air shutter may need closing slightly (less air)
Vent cap incorrect or blocked, or vent pipes leaking → adjust, clear or repair

codes: Pack under 4V; low double-beep on ON/OFF commands. Replace the batteries.
No flame after 2 tries. Verify gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset (section 10.7.1) or re-initialize (section 10.2).

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights its own pilot with an igniter. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Everyday start

Press ON/OFF on the remote. The fireplace beeps once and starts its lighting sequence. Sparking at the pilot begins about 4 seconds after you press the key.

Full lighting steps

Use these for the first start, or any time the gas has been turned off.

  1. First read the safety steps (see Safety & gas smell).
  2. Press OFF on the remote. Turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  3. Find the manual gas valve your installer fitted. Turn it clockwise to OFF.
  4. Wait 5 minutes for any gas to clear. Then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  5. Turn the valve counterclockwise to ON.
  6. Turn the electric power back on, then press ON on the remote.

Shutting the gas off

Press OFF on the remote, then turn the manual valve clockwise to OFF. If service is planned, turn off the electric power too. If the fireplace won't run, shut the gas off this way and call your service technician or gas supplier.

Turn the valve by hand only, never with tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't force it and don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs the fireplace. A single beep from the fireplace confirms each command.

  • ON/OFF turns the fireplace on or off.
  • Flame height: 6 levels. The down arrow lowers it one level at a time, all the way to off. The up arrow raises it. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, the up arrow lights it on HI.
  • Thermostat key: press it once, then set a room temperature with the arrows. Keep pressing until SMART shows for the smart thermostat, which turns the flame down as the room reaches your setting. While the smart thermostat is on, you can't adjust the flame by hand.
  • Mode key: steps to split flow (the second burner), the fan (6 speeds), the top light (6 levels) and AUX (the ember-bed light, on or off). Use the arrows to change each one.
  • Key lock: press Mode and the up arrow together. A lock icon shows.
  • °F or °C: with the fireplace off, press Thermostat and Mode together.
Fan timing: on the thermostat, the fan waits 5 minutes after the fire lights so heat can build, and keeps running about 12 minutes after it goes off. In manual mode it runs at your last setting with no delay.

To dim the ember-bed light, lift off the safety screen and turn the knob on the left side of the firebox. Clockwise is brighter, counterclockwise is dimmer.

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
Foggy glass

Condensation forms on the glass when the fireplace is first lit. That's normal for all gas fireplaces, and it disappears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during that time. It helps the paint cure faster.

Ticks, pings and creaks

Metal expands as the fireplace heats and contracts as it cools, so you may hear noises. This is normal and doesn't affect how well it works or how long it lasts.

Blue flames at first

Right after lighting, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips, the burner's air setting may need adjusting by a qualified service technician.

A gas smell is different. If you smell gas, don't light anything or touch switches. See Safety & gas smell.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is a once-a-year homeowner job. Do it only when the fireplace is completely cool. Never clean or remove hot glass.

  1. Clear a flat, stable work surface big enough for the glass frame.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. With the provided latch tool, release the 2 spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox. Tilt the top of the glass frame forward and lift it off the bottom rail.
  4. Clean the glass with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Never use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. Set the frame back on the bottom rail, latch it with the tool, and put the safety screen back.
Don't run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, or without the safety screen. Avoid striking or slamming the glass. Damaged glass is replaced as a complete assembly from Hussong Mfg., by a qualified service person.
Note: p. 53 says 2 spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox secure the glass assembly; the yearly firebox check on p. 75 says to inspect and operate the bottom latch assembly.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
modes.html:
The pilot can run two ways. You choose with the remote.

IPIspark-to-pilot
CPIcontinuous (standing) pilot

A standing pilot keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the main burner lights with less air-flow disruption.

To switch

  1. With the fireplace off, press Mode until the CPI icon shows.
  2. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow to go back to IPI. One beep confirms.

With the fireplace on, a snowflake icon on the remote's screen means CPI. No snowflake means IPI. If your pilot never goes out, it's set to CPI. Switch it to IPI.

Built-in safety timers

  • In CPI, if the main burner doesn't light for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off. Each time the burner lights, the 7-day timer starts over.
  • If the pilot stays lit continuously, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours to check its safety functions. Then it repeats your last command.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on house power. If the power goes out, a backup battery pack in the control module keeps the burner working.

Backup pack (control module)4 × AA (not included)
Remote3 × AAA (included)

During an outage

Battery backup runs the burner only. The fan, top light and ember-bed light won't work until the power comes back.

Low-battery signs

  • Remote: a battery icon appears on the screen before the batteries run out. It disappears once you replace them.
  • Backup pack: the control module gives a low double-beep when it gets an ON/OFF command, and its red light blinks once at intervals. After that it ignores commands until you replace the batteries. It beeps once when the new ones are in.

How long batteries last depends on their quality, how often the fireplace lights and, for the remote, how often you change the thermostat setting.

reset.title: Won't light? Reset it
reset.html:
Each time it's turned on, the control tries twice to light the pilot. Each try sparks for about 60 seconds, with about 35 seconds between tries. If both fail, it locks out. The red light on the control module then blinks 3 times, over and over, until it's reset.

Reset after a lockout

Use any one of these. The lighting sequence then starts again.

  • Remote: press ON/OFF to turn it off, wait about 2 seconds, press ON/OFF again.
  • Rocker switch (left side, behind the safety screen): set it to OFF, wait about 2 seconds, set it back to ON.
  • Flame arrows: press the down arrow until the screen shows OFF, wait about 2 seconds, then press the up arrow.

Quick checks

  • The rocker switch must be ON for the burner to light.
  • Make sure the gas is on. There may be more than one shut-off valve. On propane, check the tank.
  • Replace the remote and backup batteries.
  • Red light blinking 2 times means a pilot flame error. Contact your dealer.
Anything beyond these checks is for a qualified technician.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Some gas is heavier than air and settles low, so smell near the floor too.

Every day

  • The glass gets hot enough to burn. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the safety screen on. If it's damaged, replace it with the Hussong Mfg. screen made for this fireplace.
  • Watch young children closely in the room. If someone at risk lives with you, a safety gate is recommended to keep them away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from the fireplace. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Never burn wood, coal, paper, cardboard or any other solid fuel in it.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpet or bedding can mean it needs cleaning more often.

What the service visit covers

  • Firebox (yearly): vacuum out any debris.
  • Fan (every 6 months): disconnect it from power and vacuum it. The bearings are sealed and never need oil.
  • Vent system (yearly): check the vent and outside cap for soot or blockage. Air flow must never be blocked.
  • Burner and pilot (yearly): vacuum, check gas connections for leaks, and check that the burner lights within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening and that the flames are steady, not lifting or floating.
  • Glass (yearly): clean it and inspect it for cracks, scratches and nicks.

Between visits, keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that burns, and of gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

Any safety screen, guard or barrier removed for service must go back on before the fireplace is used.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. warrants this Kozy Heat gas appliance to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, to be free of defects in materials and workmanship at the time of manufacture. You don't need to send anything in to register. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model.

30 days · parts & laborpaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborall parts and material except the 30-day items
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyfirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is paid to an authorized dealer only. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer for service within 30 days.

What voids it

  • Installation by anyone other than a licensed, authorized service technician or contractor, or not installing, running and maintaining it as the manual says.
  • Removing the serial number or testing label, or altering the appliance in any way.
  • Submersion in water, or long periods of dampness or condensation.
The warranty can't be transferred. This is a summary; the full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas min / max5" / 10.5" WC
Natural gas recommended7" WC
Propane min / max12" / 13" WC
Propane recommended12" WC (Table 5.1)

Test at the valve's IN tap (A) with all other gas appliances in the house on, or at full capacity: loosen the tap screw, attach a manometer on a 1/4" I.D. hose, light pilot and burner and read. Turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose and tighten the tap screw clockwise: snug, don't over-tighten. Relight pilot and burner, then reattach the manometer to the tap (A) to verify it is completely sealed: it should read no pressure. If the reading is too high or too low, contact the gas company — only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure.

For supply-piping pressure tests above ½ psi, disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve; at ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure

Test at the valve's OUT tap (B): light the pilot, loosen the tap screw counterclockwise, attach a manometer on a 1/4" I.D. hose, light the burner and read. Turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the manometer hose and tighten the tap screw clockwise: snug, don't over-tighten. Relight pilot and burner and attach the manometer to the tap (B) to verify it is completely sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Co-axial 5" exhaust x 8" air intake. Approved (horizontal and vertical): American Metal Products (Ameri-Vent), BDM, ICC, Metal Fab (adapter 5DDA required), Olympia Chimney Supply, Selkirk and Simpson DuraVent — caps in Tables 7.1 and 7.2. Reducible to 4" x 6-5/8" with an approved reducer. Kozy Power Vent #KPV is approved (horizontal terminations only).

Horizontal (vertical + 90° elbow + cap)

24" verticalup to 24" horizontal
36" verticalup to 8' horizontal
48" verticalup to 12' horizontal
25' vertical (max)up to 25' horizontal

Basement install (24" min 5" x 8" vertical + 4" x 6-5/8" reducer + 90° + 24" max horizontal): reset the air shutters to natural gas 3/8" front / 3/8" rear, propane 1/2" front / 5/8" rear.

Vertical: 3' min to 50' max, with or without the 4" x 6-5/8" reducer. With the reducer, any 45° elbow needs a 10' minimum vertical run; up to 4 x 45°, no 90°s; subtract 18" per 45°.

Combination: termination inside the shaded area of Figure 7.2; 25' max rise + 25' max run = 50' total; max 5 x 90° — subtract 3' for each after the first; 2 x 45° may replace one 90°, subtracting 18" per 45°.

Chimney conversions (have the existing chimney inspected by a qualified chimney sweep or professional installer, and confirm the local jurisdiction allows it): both start with a 90° elbow and the 4" x 6-5/8" reducer, allow 0" to 24" of horizontal run, and take 10' min to 50' max of aluminum flex — 4" flex (retro connector, top adapter) in an existing min 7" ID Class A metal/masonry chimney, or 3" x 3" co-linear flex (coaxial to co-linear adapter) in a min 6" x 8" ID masonry or 7" ID Class A metal chimney. With 4" flex, the vent heat shield assembly must be installed when using minimum horizontal venting off the top.

Never share or connect to a chimney flue serving a separate solid-fuel appliance. Horizontal sections need 1/4" rise per 12" of travel.

The AC supply must be hot at all times — no switch in it. Shut off the household breaker before working on electrical lines. Ground per local codes, or ANSI/NFPA 70 (CSA C22.1 in Canada); the three-prong plug goes directly into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle — never cut or remove the grounding prong.

The 4-outlet junction box on the left side feeds the Kozy Power Vent, the ember bed light kit and the control module. On battery backup only the burner runs — not the fan, top light or ember bed light. Wiring schematic: Figure 9.1 (p. 60).

review.notes: Manual pages 2, 4 and 6 are blank. Not in the manual, so not checked against the catalog: efficiency (68.44% NG / 67.75% LP AFUE), weight (302 lb), heating area. Figure 2.1 (p. 9) and Figure 3.5 (p. 15) give the appliance and rough-in dimensions only as drawing labels (35¼", 44⅝", 20", 22", 43¼", 51⅝"…); the text doesn't say which is height, width or depth, so the guide points to the drawings instead of labelling them, and the catalog H/W/D (35.25 / 44.625 / 20) and view area (38-7/16" x 24 7/8") weren't compared — the only glass size in the text is the 23.75" x 35.75" glass part (p. 77). Figure 3.7's wall pass-through dimension (p. 17) and the Figure 4.1/4.5 finishing dimensions aren't transcribed either. Metric typos in figure labels (not used in the guide): 51-5/8" is printed as 1131mm (p. 9), 1311mm (pp. 14–15) and 1331mm (p. 36); 27½" as 699mm (p. 33) and 669mm (p. 40). Table 5.1 (p. 43) prints "recommended" under the propane 12" WC minimum with no separate value, while Table 11.1 (p. 70) lists propane 12"–13" WC min–max; the guide shows 12" – 13" and only the natural gas 7" WC recommendation. Wording problems left out of the guide: 10.9.5 "Turn OFF the appliance" (p. 67) repeats the turn-on wording (the guide uses p. 63's "press the wireless remote OFF button" and 10.9.5's described result); 10.9.8 split-flow steps are numbered 4–6 (p. 68); the outdoor-install cross-references read "continues on page 18" / "continued from 19" (pp. 18–19). Table 7.1 (p. 46) pairs the 5" ICC TM-5SVT cap with wind/rain shield 4SVTS, the same shield listed for the 4" TM-4SVT — possibly a typo; not used in the guide. The catalog calls the fan kit, top accent light and ember-bed light standard; the manual doesn't say standard or optional (ember-bed bulbs "included in component packet", top-light bulbs "included with this kit"). The flame-modulation, light-modulation and thermostat deactivation procedures (pp. 67–69) and the 10.3 manual-operation steps are referenced, not reproduced. Lifting/ghosting flames get two remedies in the manual — close the venturi (Fig. 11.4, p. 71; troubleshooting p. 74) or reduce vent restriction (Table 11.4, p. 72); the guide gives both, as the manual does. check_numbers: every number in the guide was found in the manual text.
